summary: Red team of the KW I extraction (Khare–Wintenberger, Serre's modularity conjecture (I), Invent. Math. 178 (2009) 485–504), read in the authors' copy (hash matches). The item-level work is careful. Every numbered statement has an item with the right locator. The library citations hold at the pins, and the §7 estimates and the §8 local calculations check out. E1–E6 are real, and the review's changes are correct. There are eight findings: four medium and four low. (1) The routing creates a cycle: Theorem 10.1(ii) stays at R27.6, but its weight-one descent is routed to ML.1, which imports Theorem 10.1 from R27.6. (2) E3's correction applies Theorem 5.1(1) at weight k(ρ̄), outside its hypothesis 2 ≤ k(ρ̄) ≤ p + 1, and omits the untwisting step (Edixhoven's weight theorem, R20.3). (3) Minimal lifts are assigned to R24.3, not LocalGaloisDeformationRings R08.6 (the owner the KW II extraction and R24.3 itself name), and the one 'missing' item on route 2 (/33) is already stated at R24.3/required-lift-types. (4) The strong form of Serre's conjecture in all cases, and the qualitative-to-refined theorem that §10 uses, have no item. Low: the residual-member facts (almost-all irreducibility, residual weights, ℓ = 2) have no item; Lemma 6.2(i) for p > 2 has no supplier; the status of Corollary 10.2(ii) conflicts with CG-20's; and (H) is described as 2-adic only.

The Springer version of record was not read; findings quote the author copy and are scoped to it.

Reading. I read the whole paper in a text extraction: abstract, contents, §§1–11 and references [1]–[46]. I rendered p. 12 (§7) at 300 dpi and confirmed the review's correction to /40: the paper prints '3/2 − (1/30) = 1.46̄' with a bar over the 6.

Coverage. Every numbered statement has an item with the right page: Theorems 1.1, 1.2(1)–(2), 3.1–3.4, 4.1(1)–(2), 5.1(1)–(4), 9.1, 10.1(i)–(ii); Definition 2.1; Lemmas 6.1, 6.2(i)–(ii), 6.3(i)–(ii), 8.2; Corollaries 8.1(i)–(ii), 10.2(i)–(ii); (L_r), (W_r), (D_r), (H); the remarks after Theorems 3.4 and 5.1, Lemma 8.2 and (H); §7 (1)–(4). Unnumbered inputs without an item: findings 4 and 5.

Topics the job lists. Serre's k(ρ̄) and N(ρ̄) (/2, /3); the double induction and killing ramification (/12–/18); weight reduction (/15, /40, /41); minimal lifts and prescribed local types (/26–/33; finding 3); potential modularity and Taylor (only through Theorem 5.1, proved in KW II, which the KW II extraction routes); modularity lifting by Wiles, Taylor–Wiles, Kisin and Skinner–Wiles (/20, /21, /48, /50); compatible systems and Fontaine–Laffaille (/22–/25; finding 5); level raising via Carayol's analogue in Theorem 5.1(4) and Diamond's lifting theorem (/31, /46–/48); the level-one case (/7, /16, /42, /43); base cases p = 2, 3, 5. KW I does not cite Tate, Serre or Brueggeman: the small primes enter through Khare's level-one theorem (/7, R26), and SmallRamificationAndAbelianVarietyBaseCases R25.2 plans Tate and Serre. I checked every hypothesis: odd, absolutely irreducible, p > 2 versus p = 2, 2 ≤ k(ρ̄) ≤ p + 1, and non-solvable image or ρ̄|_{ℚ(μ_p)} absolutely irreducible. Items /1, /8, /9, /11–/13, /17, /19–/21, /26–/31, /42–/44 and /50 match the text word for word in their hypotheses.

Mathematics re-derived. The §7 estimates: I checked (1) or (2) by exact rational arithmetic for every prime 5 ≤ p < 200,000 with P the next prime; no failures, equality exactly at p = 5 and p = 7. I derived (3) and (4) from (1) and (2) by clearing denominators. In the §8.2 inductive step, the interval for i contains a representative of every residue class mod (P − 1)/ℓ^r, so χ′ = ω_P^i can be chosen to reduce to χ. For ℓ = 2 the evenness condition is compatible, because (P − 1)/2^r is odd. Both weights i + 2 and P + 1 − i are ≤ p + 1 by (3) and (4). The mod-3 step (q = 3, χ′ = ω_{3,2}², weight 2) and the mod-5 step (q = 5, χ′ = ω_5², weight 4) are right. Diamond's list of (i, j) satisfies i + qj = m(q² − 1)/p^r, and j < i ⟺ m < p^r/2. For p = 2 the generator of the 2-part has i + j odd, so it is excluded. In §8.4, ρ′_{p′} is crystalline at p′ because k(ρ̄_{p′}) = 2, so ρ̄′_s is unramified at p′ and p′ is a legitimate t in Definition 2.1. The Lemma 8.2 conditions cover every prime r ≤ p′ − 1 that Definition 2.1(ii) needs for ρ̄′_s. In Lemma 6.3(i), q ≡ 1 mod 8 and mod every ramified s forces q to split in any quadratic field unramified outside those primes. In Corollary 8.1(ii), reduction mod t of the t-group ρ(I_q) is unipotent, so N(ρ̄_t) = q.

Source issues. E1, E2, E5 and E6 are real misprints, confirmed in the text (pp. 9, 19). E3 is a real gap, but its correction is incomplete (finding 2). E4 is real (p. 14, 'Choose a prime divisior ℓ^r||(P − 1)' under the hypothesis 'at most divisible by r primes'). I looked for further mistakes in §§2–10 and found none beyond these. The corrections the paper makes to the literature (Khare's Corollary 1.2 reference; Skinner's correction to Skinner–Wiles) are correctly recorded as mistakes in those sources.

findings.claim: The correction recorded for the gap E3 is incomplete for odd p. It reads: 'otherwise Theorem 5.1(1) gives a lift minimally ramified away from p and crystalline of weight k(ρ̄) at p …, Theorem 4.1 makes it modular, and its newform has weight k(ρ̄) and level N(ρ̄)'. But Theorem 5.1 assumes 2 ≤ k(ρ̄) ≤ p + 1 when p > 2, and for odd p Serre's weight ranges over 2 ≤ k(ρ̄) ≤ p² − 1. The paper notes this: only some twist ρ̄ ⊗ χ_p^i has weight in [2, p + 1]. For k(ρ̄) > p + 1 the argument proves only that ρ̄ ⊗ χ_p^i arises from S_{k(ρ̄⊗χ^i)}(Γ_1(N(ρ̄))). Going back to ρ̄ at weight exactly k(ρ̄) needs a further step: twisting mod p forms (θ-operator and Serre's twisting rule for k), Edixhoven's weight theorem, and the Deligne–Serre lifting of the resulting mod p eigenform of weight k(ρ̄) ≥ 2. Concrete case: if ρ̄|_{I_p} ≅ 1 ⊕ χ̄_p (Serre weight 2) and p ≥ 5, then (ρ̄ ⊗ χ̄_p)|_{I_p} ≅ χ̄_p ⊕ χ̄_p², whose weight by Serre's recipe (k = 1 + pa + b with a = 1, b = 2) is p + 3 > p + 1. Theorem 5.1 does not apply to it. The review's reason for E3 adds '(after a twist into [2, p + 1] for p odd)' but leaves the correction text unchanged and does not supply the untwisting. The atlas node R27.4/strong-form-by-minimal-lifts likewise concludes only 'for odd p after the twist'. So item /8's note, 'the blueprint supplies it in R27.4/strong-form-by-minimal-lifts', overstates what that node proves. The missing step is planned elsewhere, at SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation R20.3 ('the Edixhoven/Serre weight theorem … the effect of twisting') and R27.6 ('R20's optimisation'), but neither the errata entry nor item /8 names it.
findings.evidence: Paper p. 2: 'It is an important feature of the weight k(ρ̄), for p > 2, that if χ_p is the mod p cyclotomic character, then for some i ∈ Z, 2 ≤ k(ρ̄ ⊗ χ_p^i) ≤ p + 1.' p. 9, Theorem 5.1: 'Consider a S-type representation ρ̄ with 2 ≤ k(ρ̄) ≤ p + 1 when p > 2.' p. 6: 'Then by Theorem 3.4, and the remark after it, we get Theorem 1.2.' Serre, Duke Math. J. 54 (1987), §2: the weight lies in [2, p² − 1] (for tame level-one inertia χ^a ⊕ χ^b with 0 ≤ a < b ≤ p − 2, k = 1 + pa + b). Atlas node ClassicalSerreModularity:R27.4/strong-form-by-minimal-lifts: 'Then ρ̄ arises from S_{k(ρ̄)}(Γ₁(N(ρ̄))) (for odd p after the twist that puts 2 ≤ k(ρ̄) ≤ p + 1)'. SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation:R20.3 stage text: 'Prove the Edixhoven/Serre weight theorem … State the exact conclusion at weight p+1 and the effect of twisting.'
findings.fix: Amend E3's correction to read: '… otherwise choose i with 2 ≤ k(ρ̄ ⊗ χ_p^i) ≤ p + 1 (p odd; i = 0 when p = 2); Theorem 5.1(1) gives a lift of ρ̄ ⊗ χ_p^i minimally ramified away from p and crystalline of weight k(ρ̄ ⊗ χ_p^i), Theorem 4.1 makes it modular, and its newform has level N(ρ̄) (twisting by χ_p leaves the prime-to-p conductor unchanged). Untwist: ρ̄ is then modular of level N(ρ̄) prime to p, and Edixhoven's weight theorem (with θ-operators and the Deligne–Serre lifting lemma) gives a newform of weight k(ρ̄) and level N(ρ̄).' Change item /8's note to cite SerreWeightAndLevelOptimisation:R20.3 and ClassicalSerreModularity:R27.6 as well as R27.4/strong-form-by-minimal-lifts, and say which step each supplies. Update the report's E3 row. Send the same amendment to the ClassicalSerreModularity packet's E9, and a request that R27.4/strong-form-by-minimal-lifts either import the untwisting from R20.3 or state its conclusion only for the twist.

findings.claim: Two facts about compatible systems are used at almost every step of §§8–10 ('by almost strict compatibility'), but no item states them. (a) Residual irreducibility: for an irreducible compatible system, ρ̄_λ is absolutely irreducible for almost all λ (§8.4; §10.1, 'it is easy to see …'). (b) The Serre weight of the residual members: k(ρ̄_ℓ) = 2 when ρ_ℓ is crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights (1, 0), for ℓ odd (Fontaine–Laffaille/Raynaud) and for ℓ = 2 (Breuil–Kisin, finite flatness, Serre's p = 2 definition); and k(ρ̄_λ) = a + 1 for large ℓ in §10.1. These facts are used in §8.2 ('k(ρ̄_2) = 2 by almost strictly compatibility as ρ̄_2 is irreducible'), in §8.3 and in §8.4 ('ρ̄_{p′} is of weight 2 by almost strict compatibility'). They are planned: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.6/residual-members parts (ii) and (v), with FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4 for ℓ = 2. But part (v) assumes ℓ ≠ 2, and the ℓ = 2 case that §8.2 needs is only item /51's p-divisible-group statement, stated as a remark about (H).
findings.evidence: Paper p. 13 (§8.2, mod 3): 'k(ρ̄_2) = 2 by almost strictly compatibility as ρ̄_2 is irreducible'. p. 17 (§8.4): 'As (ρ_λ) is an irreducible compatible system, almost all the residual representations that arise from it are absolutely irreducible … Note that for p′ ∉ S ∪ {p, 2}, ρ̄_{p′} is of weight 2 by almost strict compatibility.' p. 20: 'it is easy to see that ρ̄_λ is irreducible for almost all λ'. Node R24.6/residual-members: '(ii) ρ̄_ι is absolutely irreducible for almost all ι … (v) If ℓ is outside the ramification set, ℓ ≠ 2 and a − b + 1 ≤ ℓ − 1, then … k(ρ̄_ι) = a − b + 1 up to twist (Fontaine–Laffaille).'
findings.fix: Add an item 'Residual members of an almost strictly compatible system' for (a) and (b), with locators pp. 13, 15–17, 20, planned at PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.6 (residual-members) and FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4. Put it on route 2, and note that the ℓ = 2 case of (b) (crystalline of Hodge–Tate weights (1, 0) ⇒ ρ̄_2 finite flat ⇒ k(ρ̄_2) = 2) is outside residual-members (v) and should be requested there.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-I.result.json: summary ('Hypothesis (H) is modularity of odd, potentially Barsotti–Tate, 2-adic lifts …') and research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-I.md, 'What the paper proves'; item PAPER-KHARE-WINTENBERGER-09-I/50 (note)
findings.claim: The summary and report call (H) a 2-adic statement. The paper states (H) for every p ('a continuous, odd, irreducible, p-adic representation'), and item /50 states it that way. Only its application in §9 is 2-adic, and only the 2-adic case is Kisin's [28]. Item /50's note ('Proved by Kisin, Modularity of 2-adic Barsotti–Tate representations') attributes all of (H) to that paper. For odd p, (H) follows from Theorem 4.1(2)(ii) (Kisin [26]): non-solvable image forces ρ̄|_{G_ℚ(μ_p)} to be absolutely irreducible, since otherwise ρ̄ is induced from the quadratic subfield of ℚ(μ_p) and is projectively dihedral. The atlas node GL2ModularityLifting:R22.6/hypothesis-h states (H) only for p = 2 and says so explicitly.
findings.evidence: Paper p. 18: 'Hypothesis (H): Let ρ : G_Q → GL_2(O) be a continuous, odd, irreducible, p-adic representation, such that: (i) the residual representation ρ̄ has non-solvable image, and ρ̄ is modular; (ii) ρ is unramified outside a finite set of primes, is of weight 2 and potentially crystalline at p. Then ρ is modular.' Abstract, p. 1: 'a modularity statement for 2-adic lifts of modular mod 2 representations. This statement is now a theorem of Kisin [28].' p. 7, Theorem 4.1(2)(ii).
findings.fix: In the summary and report say: '(H), stated for every p, is used only at p = 2, where Kisin proved it; for odd p it is Theorem 4.1(2)(ii)'. Add the same sentence to /50's note, and cite GL2ModularityLifting:R22.5/kisin-potentially-bt-lifting for odd p beside R22.6.
